investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 14:04 and 14:12 UTC on 2026-07-22 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested peer-pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both were already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the Unschedulable state and the remote VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that the two peer-pod-capable nodes are fully consumed and preemption cannot free capacity. Because the agent pod never scheduled, createAgent() in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885) never returned a VM identity, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the expected-output contract to fail completely. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.title: model-matrix eval failure: aura-gpt-5-5 returned HTTP 502 due to upstream Anthropic 429 rate-limit error
investigation.summary: The model-matrix smoke-test eval failed because the runtime test call for model aura-gpt-5-5 received a 502 Bad Gateway response wrapping an Anthropic API 429 Too Many Requests (rate_limit) error. One of two configured models (aura-claude-sonnet-4-6) passed cleanly; only aura-gpt-5-5 failed, causing the allPassed and failedModelCount assertions to be violated. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a transient upstream rate-limit condition at the time of the run; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The AURA harness runtime test endpoint (POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test) returned HTTP 502 for model aura-gpt-5-5. The 502 body explicitly identifies the cause as a rate_limit error: the Anthropic API returned 429 Too Many Requests with message "AURA is temporarily unable to reach the model provider. This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits. Please try again shortly." The provider and resolvedModel fields in the result for aura-gpt-5-5 are both null, confirming the request never reached a successful model resolution. The failure is localized to the aura-gpt-5-5 model slot in the desktop-nightly-macos-aarch64 eval run at 2026-07-22T14:02:58Z; the sibling model aura-claude-sonnet-4-6 succeeded in the same run, and no sibling checks share this failure, making a broad infrastructure outage unlikely.

investigation.title: Image Generation Eval Failure: OpenAI Billing Hard Limit Reached on /api/generate/image/stream
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API returned a hard billing limit error (code: billing_hard_limit_reached) when the eval runner called /api/generate/image/stream. investigation.rootCause: The OpenAI account or API key used by the eval runner has hit its billing hard limit. When the runner called /api/generate/image/stream (evidence: source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1977-1985), the upstream OpenAI image generation API rejected the request with error type "billing_limit_user_error" and code "billing_hard_limit_reached". The AURA backend propagated this as a generation_error SSE frame (evidence: failed-check.evidence), which caused the stream to terminate without emitting a generation_completed frame or an image artifact URL. This is an eval infrastructure / external dependency failure localized to the /api/generate/image/stream endpoint and the OpenAI billing account bound to the eval environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Image Generation Eval Failure: OpenAI Billing Hard Limit Reached on /api/generate/image/stream
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API returned a hard billing limit error (code: billing_hard_limit_reached) when the eval runner called /api/generate/image/stream. The stream terminated with a generation_error frame instead of a generation_completed frame, causing both required contract assertions to fail: frameTypes did not contain "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent remained false.

The AURA backend propagated this as a generation_error SSE frame (evidence: failed-check.evidence), which caused the stream to terminate without emitting a generation_completed frame or an image artifact URL. This is an eval infrastructure / external dependency failure localized to the /api/generate/image/stream endpoint and the OpenAI billing account bound to the eval environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: model-matrix eval failure: aura-gpt-5-5 returned HTTP 502 due to upstream Anthropic 429 rate-limit error
investigations.summary: The model-matrix smoke-test eval failed because the runtime test call for model aura-gpt-5-5 received a 502 Bad Gateway response wrapping an Anthropic API 429 Too Many Requests (rate_limit) error. One of two configured models (aura-claude-sonnet-4-6) passed cleanly; only aura-gpt-5-5 failed, causing the allPassed and failedModelCount assertions to be violated. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a transient upstream rate-limit condition at the time of the run; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The AURA harness runtime test endpoint (POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test) returned HTTP 502 for model aura-gpt-5-5. The 502 body explicitly identifies the cause as a rate_limit error: the Anthropic API returned 429 Too Many Requests with message "AURA is temporarily unable to reach the model provider. This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits. Please try again shortly." The provider and resolvedModel fields in the result for aura-gpt-5-5 are both null, confirming the request never reached a successful model resolution. The failure is localized to the aura-gpt-5-5 model slot in the desktop-nightly-macos-aarch64 eval run at 2026-07-22T14:02:58Z; the sibling model aura-claude-sonnet-4-6 succeeded in the same run, and no sibling checks share this failure, making a broad infrastructure outage unlikely.
proof: failed-check.evidence: results[1] for aura-gpt-5-5 shows ok=false, provider=null, resolvedModel=null, and error containing 'POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test failed with 502' and 'harness runtime test failed (rate_limit): Anthropic API error: 429 Too Many Requests'.

failed-check.evidence: results[0] for aura-claude-sonnet-4-6 shows ok=true, provider=anthropic, resolvedModel=aura-claude-sonnet-4-6, messageSample='hello from aura', confirming the eval harness itself was functional for the passing model.

failed-check.message: '1/2 models returned the expected response; Expected evidence assertion failed: allPassed expected true but got false; failedModelCount expected 0 but got 1' directly maps to the two violated assertions in the expected-output contract.
expected-output.contract: assertions require allPassed=true and failedModelCount=0; the run produced allPassed=false and failedModelCount=1, violating both.
failed-check.evidence: failedModels=['aura-gpt-5-5'] isolates the failure to a single model.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=83213, well within the warningLatencyMs=180000 and outageLatencyMs=360000 thresholds defined in source.infra/evals/status/features.json:249, so latency is not a contributing factor.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1931-1936: the runner iterates over args.models and calls the runtime test endpoint for each; the 502 was returned for the aura-gpt-5-5 iteration only.
possibleCauses: Most likely (high evidence): Transient Anthropic API rate-limit (429) at the time of the eval run caused the AURA backend to return a 502 to the harness for the aura-gpt-5-5 model slot. The error message explicitly states this is a temporary, server-side condition unrelated to account or credits.

Possible (medium evidence): The aura-gpt-5-5 model may be routed through a different Anthropic API quota bucket or key than aura-claude-sonnet-4-6, making it more susceptible to rate exhaustion during concurrent or high-frequency eval runs.

Possible (low evidence): The AURA backend gateway layer may have a per-model or per-provider retry/timeout policy that differs between model identifiers, causing aura-gpt-5-5 to surface the 429 as a 502 without retry while aura-claude-sonnet-4-6 succeeded. No source evidence is available to confirm or deny this.

Unlikely (no supporting evidence): A misconfiguration of the aura-gpt-5-5 model entry in the eval model list or backend routing table. The error body shows the request reached the Anthropic API and received a valid 429 response, indicating routing was not broken.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 14:04 and 14:12 UTC on 2026-07-22 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested peer-pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both were already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the Unschedulable state and the remote VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that the two peer-pod-capable nodes are fully consumed and preemption cannot free capacity. Because the agent pod never scheduled, createAgent() in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885) never returned a VM identity, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the expected-output contract to fail completely. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
